data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A content-addressed derivation cache with durable provenance anchors achieves equivalent safety without a global log, provided the anchor record includes the full dependency closure, a tombstone-resistant witness attestation, and a seal-of-derivation signed by the workspace holder.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The anchor store experiences split-brain where a valid anchor is invisible to the reclaimer but visible to readers, permitting silent displacement.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Hash collisions in the content-addressed store allow distinct evidence to share an identifier.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The witness attestation relies on synchronized clocks and suffers skew-induced false negatives as in SRC_008.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Completed evidence is externalized as a content-addressed object. The holder writes a provenance anchor to a durable, replicated key-value store keyed by problem-id, containing (content-hash, input-hashes, timestamp-witness, holder-epoch). Reclamation only proceeds if a causal cut shows no anchor for the problem-id and the holder's heartbeat lease has expired. Because the evidence is content-addressed, displacement is detectable: recompute yields the same hash, revealing a silent displacement after the fact.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
